items.prompt: A platform team compares three access models for a supported PaaS service. The service must keep its normal public endpoint and DNS name, identify calls by Azure client subnet, and require no private IP in the consumer VNet. Which model matches all three constraints?
constraints: A service endpoint extends a subnet's identity to a supported Azure service over the Azure backbone; the service still uses its public endpoint and DNS name.
Enable the endpoint on the client subnet and configure the resource firewall; do not treat it as a private IP deployment.

options.text: Use a virtual network service endpoint on each approved client subnet with matching service-side virtual network firewall rules.
Use a private endpoint because it preserves a public-only address model.
Use App Service VNet integration on the PaaS service to authenticate every client subnet.
Use Azure Bastion because its dedicated subnet identifies every application request.

feedback.Reason: Service endpoints preserve the public service endpoint while extending subnet identity to the supported service; neither a consumer private NIC nor App Service worker egress is required.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Service endpoints preserve the public service endpoint while extending subnet identity to the supported service; neither a consumer private NIC nor App Service worker egress is required.
Details.scenarioApplication: Use a virtual network service endpoint on each approved client subnet with matching service-side virtual network firewall rules.
Details.errorCorrection: A private endpoint creates a consumer-side private NIC and changes the intended DNS path to a private address. VNet integration is app-originated outbound connectivity, not a general service-side subnet admission model. Bastion brokers administrative RDP and SSH sessions rather than PaaS data-plane calls.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A service endpoint extends a subnet's identity to a supported Azure service over the Azure backbone; the service still uses its public endpoint and DNS name.
Details.transfer: Enable the endpoint on the client subnet and configure the resource firewall; do not treat it as a private IP deployment.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.B: A private endpoint creates a consumer-side private NIC and changes the intended DNS path to a private address.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.C: VNet integration is app-originated outbound connectivity, not a general service-side subnet admission model.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.D: Bastion brokers administrative RDP and SSH sessions rather than PaaS data-plane calls.

options.text: Use a service endpoint because it creates an approvable consumer NIC.

Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A private endpoint is a NIC with a private IP in a consumer VNet that connects to a specific Private Link resource subresource.
Details.transfer: Plan the target subresource, approval state, DNS, subnet policies, and client routing as separate controls.
